Night trains are coming back. From December, sleeper services will run again between three pairs of European capitals, after operators reported that demand for overnight rail travel has roughly doubled since 2022.

The new routes use refurbished carriages with private compartments, showers and a small dining car, and tickets will go on sale next month at prices that operators say are competitive with budget airlines once hotel costs are included.

Rail campaigners welcomed the announcement, but warned that high track access charges and a shortage of rolling stock still make it hard for companies to expand quickly. Several routes that were announced two years ago have yet to start running.

Passengers interviewed on the platform at the launch event said the main attraction was avoiding airports. "You go to sleep in one city and wake up in the centre of another," said one traveller. "It feels like the future, even though it is really the past."
